run-ref: 8df239fa0d13c41f1eef8b5a7d78f318

The support desk of a document-processing service is working through a live incident with you, one question at a time. Your tools give read-only access to the service's job-event journals, its configuration change history, queue statistics and the operations playbook. Use them to establish the facts.

Since a little after 11:00 UTC customers say their uploaded documents sit in processing and then come back rejected. Which pipeline component is rejecting the jobs, and at what time, as that component's journal records it, did it reject the first one?

Reply format: after any explanation, put a fenced ```json block containing one object with exactly these fields, and nothing else:
- rejecting_component: the name on its own, as the tool output writes it
- first_rejection_time: the time exactly as the journal writes it
Copy values verbatim from the tool output (no rounding or reformatting), and put no labels, notes or other text inside a value.

function_tools.description: Returns the job-event journal of one component for one hour, a page at a time (earliest events first; each page's first line gives the page count for that hour). The support desk of a document-processing service is working through a live incident with you, one question at a time. Your tools give read-only access to the service's job-event journals, its configuration change history, queue statistics and the operations playbook. Use them to establish the facts.

Since a little after 11:00 UTC customers say their uploaded documents sit in processing and then come back rejected. Which pipeline component is rejecting the jobs, and at what time, as that component's journal records it, did it reject the first one?

Reply format: after any explanation, put a fenced ```json block containing one object with exactly these fields, and nothing else:
- rejecting_component: the name on its own, as the tool output writes it
- first_rejection_time: the time exactly as the journal writes it
Copy values verbatim from the tool output (no rounding or reformatting), and put no labels, notes or other text inside a value.

<summary_of_earlier_work>
- Task: identify which pipeline component is rejecting uploaded-document jobs (customers report stuck/rejected processing since ~11:00 UTC) and the exact journal timestamp of its first rejection.

Investigation steps:
- Ran queue_stats for all six pipeline queues (q.heath-scan, q.kelp-split, q.pike-ocr, q.basalt-extract, q.slate-index, q.ember-notify) for hour 2026-11-15 11:00-12:00, 10-min buckets.
- Results: all queues showed 0 rejected except q.basalt-extract, which had rejected counts: 11:00=0, 11:10=0, 11:20=0, 11:30=12, 11:40=43, 11:50=45 (hour total rejected=100, requeued=253, done=1457, enqueued=1578). Depth and oldest_wait_s also spiked for basalt-extract starting ~11:20 (depth 700-819, oldest_wait_s up to 1440s at 11:30). q.slate-index showed high oldest_wait_s/depth too but zero rejections (likely downstream backpressure effect, not the rejecting component). Other queues (heath-scan, kelp-split, pike-ocr, ember-notify) were normal throughout.
- Conclusion: q.basalt-extract (component name "basalt-extract") is the one rejecting jobs; others are unaffected or just backed up as a side effect.

Journal reading (component=basalt-extract, hour=11:00), paginated (15 pages total):
- Page 1 (seq 131664-131721, times 11:00:03-11:04:22): normal received/leased/progress/completed events only, no retries or rejections.
- Page 8 (seq 132070-132127, times 11:28:46-11:32:52): normal activity until seq 132117-132118 at 11:32:16/17 where first "retry" events appear: "worker process ended unexpectedly; job requeued (attempt 1 of 3)" for jobs J-JC4E3ARA and J-SMBT4DH2. More retries (attempt 2 of 3) follow at 11:32:44 and 11:32:48.
- Page 9 (seq 132128-132185, times 11:32:52-11:35:58): retry events continue to multiply rapidly (many jobs hitting attempt 1/2/3), no job-rejected events yet on this page.
- Page 10 (seq 132186-132243, times 11:35:59-11:40:12): retries continue; first "job-rejected" event appears at seq 132199: "11:37:03.413 | J-KGYBCJFY | tn-9553 | job-rejected | rejected after 3 worker crashes; customer notified" — this follows job J-KGYBCJFY's 4th retry attempt (attempt "4 of 3") logged at 132195 (11:36:45.485), and an earlier attempt 3 of 3 at 132190 (11:36:22.462). Second rejection follows immediately at 132200: 11:37:04.707 (J-RWNVKMEE). Many more job-rejected events follow throughout page 10 (11:37:30, 11:37:41, 11:37:52, 11:38:02, 11:38:09, 11:38:48, 11:38:55, 11:39:06, 11:39:07, 11:39:22, 11:40:08), confirming sustained rejection pattern starting at 11:37:03.413.

Root cause pattern identified: workers crashing ("worker process ended unexpectedly") causing requeue retries; after 3 failed attempts the job is marked job-rejected and customer notified. This started around 11:32 (first retries) and first actual rejection logged at 11:37:03.413.

Hypothesis confirmed: basalt-extract is the rejecting component; first rejection timestamp per its journal = 11:37:03.413 (seq 132199, job J-KGYBCJFY, tenant tn-9553).

No unresolved questions remain for this answer; ready to finalize.

```

The support desk of a document-processing service is working through a live incident with you, one question at a time. Your tools give read-only access to the service's job-event journals, its configuration change history, queue statistics and the operations playbook. Use them to establish the facts.

Since a little after 11:00 UTC customers say their uploaded documents sit in processing and then come back rejected. Which pipeline component is rejecting the jobs, and at what time, as that component's journal records it, did it reject the first one?

Reply format: after any explanation, put a fenced ```json block containing one object with exactly these fields, and nothing else:
- rejecting_component: the name on its own, as the tool output writes it
- first_rejection_time: the time exactly as the journal writes it
Copy values verbatim from the tool output (no rounding or reformatting), and put no labels, notes or other text inside a value.

<summary_of_earlier_work>
- Task: identify which pipeline component is rejecting uploaded-document jobs (customers report stuck/rejected processing since ~11:00 UTC) and the exact journal timestamp of its first rejection.

Investigation steps:
- Ran queue_stats for all six pipeline queues (q.heath-scan, q.kelp-split, q.pike-ocr, q.basalt-extract, q.slate-index, q.ember-notify) for hour 2026-11-15 11:00-12:00, 10-min buckets.
- Results: all queues showed 0 rejected except q.basalt-extract, which had rejected counts: 11:00=0, 11:10=0, 11:20=0, 11:30=12, 11:40=43, 11:50=45 (hour total rejected=100, requeued=253, done=1457, enqueued=1578). Depth and oldest_wait_s also spiked for basalt-extract starting ~11:20 (depth 700-819, oldest_wait_s up to 1440s at 11:30). q.slate-index showed high oldest_wait_s/depth too but zero rejections (likely downstream backpressure effect, not the rejecting component). Other queues (heath-scan, kelp-split, pike-ocr, ember-notify) were normal throughout.
- Conclusion: q.basalt-extract (component name "basalt-extract") is the one rejecting jobs; others are unaffected or just backed up as a side effect.

Journal reading (component=basalt-extract, hour=11:00), paginated (15 pages total):
- Page 1 (seq 131664-131721, times 11:00:03-11:04:22): normal received/leased/progress/completed events only, no retries or rejections.
- Page 8 (seq 132070-132127, times 11:28:46-11:32:52): normal activity until seq 132117-132118 at 11:32:16/17 where first "retry" events appear: "worker process ended unexpectedly; job requeued (attempt 1 of 3)" for jobs J-JC4E3ARA and J-SMBT4DH2. More retries (attempt 2 of 3) follow at 11:32:44 and 11:32:48.
- Page 9 (seq 132128-132185, times 11:32:52-11:35:58): retry events continue to multiply rapidly (many jobs hitting attempt 1/2/3), no job-rejected events yet on this page.
- Page 10 (seq 132186-132243, times 11:35:59-11:40:12): retries continue; first "job-rejected" event appears at seq 132199: "11:37:03.413 | J-KGYBCJFY | tn-9553 | job-rejected | rejected after 3 worker crashes; customer notified" — this follows job J-KGYBCJFY's 4th retry attempt (attempt "4 of 3") logged at 132195 (11:36:45.485), and an earlier attempt 3 of 3 at 132190 (11:36:22.462). Second rejection follows immediately at 132200: 11:37:04.707 (J-RWNVKMEE). Many more job-rejected events follow throughout page 10 (11:37:30, 11:37:41, 11:37:52, 11:38:02, 11:38:09, 11:38:48, 11:38:55, 11:39:06, 11:39:07, 11:39:22, 11:40:08), confirming sustained rejection pattern starting at 11:37:03.413.

Root cause pattern identified: workers crashing ("worker process ended unexpectedly") causing requeue retries; after 3 failed attempts the job is marked job-rejected and customer notified. This started around 11:32 (first retries) and first actual rejection logged at 11:37:03.413.

Hypothesis confirmed: basalt-extract is the rejecting component; first rejection timestamp per its journal = 11:37:03.413 (seq 132199, job J-KGYBCJFY, tenant tn-9553).

No unresolved questions remain for this answer; ready to finalize.

The support desk of a document-processing service is working through a live incident with you, one question at a time. Your tools give read-only access to the service's job-event journals, its configuration change history, queue statistics and the operations playbook. Use them to establish the facts.

Since a little after 11:00 UTC customers say their uploaded documents sit in processing and then come back rejected. Which pipeline component is rejecting the jobs, and at what time, as that component's journal records it, did it reject the first one?

Reply format: after any explanation, put a fenced ```json block containing one object with exactly these fields, and nothing else:
- rejecting_component: the name on its own, as the tool output writes it
- first_rejection_time: the time exactly as the journal writes it
Copy values verbatim from the tool output (no rounding or reformatting), and put no labels, notes or other text inside a value.

<summary_of_earlier_work>
- Task: identify which pipeline component is rejecting uploaded-document jobs (customers report stuck/rejected processing since ~11:00 UTC) and the exact journal timestamp of its first rejection.

Investigation steps:
- Ran queue_stats for all six pipeline queues (q.heath-scan, q.kelp-split, q.pike-ocr, q.basalt-extract, q.slate-index, q.ember-notify) for hour 2026-11-15 11:00-12:00, 10-min buckets.
- Results: all queues showed 0 rejected except q.basalt-extract, which had rejected counts: 11:00=0, 11:10=0, 11:20=0, 11:30=12, 11:40=43, 11:50=45 (hour total rejected=100, requeued=253, done=1457, enqueued=1578). Depth and oldest_wait_s also spiked for basalt-extract starting ~11:20 (depth 700-819, oldest_wait_s up to 1440s at 11:30). q.slate-index showed high oldest_wait_s/depth too but zero rejections (likely downstream backpressure effect, not the rejecting component). Other queues (heath-scan, kelp-split, pike-ocr, ember-notify) were normal throughout.
- Conclusion: q.basalt-extract (component name "basalt-extract") is the one rejecting jobs; others are unaffected or just backed up as a side effect.

Journal reading (component=basalt-extract, hour=11:00), paginated (15 pages total):
- Page 1 (seq 131664-131721, times 11:00:03-11:04:22): normal received/leased/progress/completed events only, no retries or rejections.
- Page 8 (seq 132070-132127, times 11:28:46-11:32:52): normal activity until seq 132117-132118 at 11:32:16/17 where first "retry" events appear: "worker process ended unexpectedly; job requeued (attempt 1 of 3)" for jobs J-JC4E3ARA and J-SMBT4DH2. More retries (attempt 2 of 3) follow at 11:32:44 and 11:32:48.

run-ref: 8df239fa0d13c41f1eef8b5a7d78f318

The support desk of a document-processing service is working through a live incident with you, one question at a time. Your tools give read-only access to the service's job-event journals, its configuration change history, queue statistics and the operations playbook. Use them to establish the facts.

Since a little after 11:00 UTC customers say their uploaded documents sit in processing and then come back rejected. Which pipeline component is rejecting the jobs, and at what time, as that component's journal records it, did it reject the first one?

Reply format: after any explanation, put a fenced ```json block containing one object with exactly these fields, and nothing else:
- rejecting_component: the name on its own, as the tool output writes it
- first_rejection_time: the time exactly as the journal writes it
Copy values verbatim from the tool output (no rounding or reformatting), and put no labels, notes or other text inside a value.

<summary_of_earlier_work>
- Task chain (same incident):
  Q1 answered: rejecting_component=basalt-extract, first_rejection_time=11:37:03.413 (journal seq 132199, job J-KGYBCJFY, tenant tn-9553, "rejected after 3 worker crashes; customer notified").
  Q2 answered: faulty_change=CHG-43068 (basalt-extract, 2026-11-15 10:42 UTC, team-Sable, "set worker.memory_limit_mb: 4096 -> 384", note: "align worker settings with the new capacity plan"). Confirmed via list_changes across all 7 components in 2hr window before 11:37; only impactful non-log-level change. Other changes were log_level tweaks, deemed irrelevant. ember-notify CHG-70782 (11:21 UTC, retry_backoff_ms 500->800) judged not causal.
  Q3 answered: rejected_jobs=100 (queue_stats q.basalt-extract 11:00-12:00 UTC, "rejected 100").

- Q4 (current, in progress): "Quote one line from that component's [basalt-extract] 11:00-12:00 UTC journal that states the configuration setting behind the problem, with its value." Need exact verbatim journal line (not the change-log CHG-43068 entry) naming the setting (likely worker.memory_limit_mb) and value (384), as logged by basalt-extract itself.

- Journal pages read so far (component=basalt-extract, hour=11:00, 15 pages total):
  - Pages 1-3 (seq 131664-131837, 11:00:03-11:10:18): normal only, no crashes.
  - Pages 6-7 (seq 131954-132069, 11:20:02-11:28:45): all normal (received/leased/progress/completed), no retries or setting mentions.
  - Page 8 (seq 132070-132127, 11:28:46-11:32:50): normal until 11:32:16 when first "retry" events appear ("worker process ended unexpectedly; job requeued (attempt 1 of 3)" for J-JC4E3ARA, J-SMBT4DH2); more retries (attempt 2 of 3) at 11:32:44, 11:32:48. No setting/value mentioned.
  - Page 9 (seq 132128-132185, 11:32:52-11:35:58): retries proliferate across many jobs (attempts 1-2 of 3), still only generic "worker process ended unexpectedly" message, no setting/value cited.
  - Page 10 (seq 132186-132243, 11:35:59-11:40:12): mix of retries, leased/received/completed, and first job-rejected events starting at 132199 (11:37:03.413, J-KGYBCJFY) through several more (J-RWNVKMEE, J-GJGS3ZKK, J-K6QMZHSZ, J-MZMFB6AK, J-MD6Y4W23, J-8SAWKQ6Z, J-7SS5EXV9, J-4Y2Q63WN, J-FKTTC9E3, J-P6XD8T83, J-R55CVGVM, J-YYMQRQCA), all with detail "rejected after 3 worker crashes; customer notified" — no explicit setting/value named on any line so far.

- Not yet read: pages 4, 5 (seq ~131838-131953, roughly 11:10-11:20) and pages 11-15 (seq 132244 onward, 11:40:12 to end of hour).

- Findings so far: No journal line in basalt-extract's own log (pages 1-3, 6-10) explicitly names a configuration setting or value; all crash/retry/rejection lines use generic phrasing ("worker process ended unexpectedly", "rejected after 3 worker crashes; customer notified"). The setting/value (worker.memory_limit_mb: 4096->384) is only confirmed via the separate change-log tool (CHG-43068), which cannot be used for this answer since the question asks for a journal line.

- Next steps: read remaining unread pages 4, 5, and 11-15 of basalt-extract's 11:00 journal, searching for any line (possibly a startup/config-reload/diagnostic/OOM line) that explicitly states a configuration setting name and value. If none found in these ranges either, may need to reconsider whether such a line exists elsewhere (e.g., different hour, or a one-time startup/reload event near 10:42 when CHG-43068 took effect — check if that falls within the 11:00 hour window or earlier hour journal).
</summary_of_earlier_work>

The question you are working on now:

Quote one line from that component's 11:00-12:00 UTC journal that states the configuration setting behind the problem, with its value.

Reply format: after any explanation, put a fenced ```json block containing one object with exactly these fields, and nothing else:
- evidence_event: one complete journal line, copied exactly
Copy values verbatim from the tool output (no rounding or reformatting), and put no labels, notes or other text inside a value.

parts.content:
<task>
Since a little after 11:00 UTC customers say their uploaded documents sit in processing and then come back rejected. Which pipeline component is rejecting the jobs, and at what time, as that component's journal records it, did it reject the first one?

Reply format: after any explanation, put a fenced ```json block containing one object with exactly these fields, and nothing else:
- rejecting_component: the name on its own, as the tool output writes it
- first_rejection_time: the time exactly as the journal writes it
Copy values verbatim from the tool output (no rounding or reformatting), and put no labels, notes or other text inside a value.
</task>

  Q1 answered: rejecting_component=basalt-extract, first_rejection_time=11:37:03.413 (journal seq 132199, job J-KGYBCJFY, tenant tn-9553, "rejected after 3 worker crashes; customer notified").
  Q2 answered: faulty_change=CHG-43068 (basalt-extract, 2026-11-15 10:42 UTC, team-Sable, "set worker.memory_limit_mb: 4096 -> 384", note: "align worker settings with the new capacity plan"). Confirmed via list_changes across all 7 components in 2hr window before 11:37; only impactful non-log-level change.   Q3 answered: rejected_jobs=100 (queue_stats q.basalt-extract 11:00-12:00 UTC, "rejected 100").

- Q4 (current, in progress): "Quote one line from that component's [basalt-extract] 11:00-12:00 UTC journal that states the configuration setting behind the problem, with its value." Need exact verbatim journal line (not the change-log CHG-43068 entry) naming the setting (likely worker.memory_limit_mb) and value (384), as logged by basalt-extract itself.

- Journal pages read so far (component=basalt-extract, hour=11:00, 15 pages total):
  - Pages 1-3 (seq 131664-131837, 11:00:03-11:10:18): normal only, no crashes.
  - Pages 6-7 (seq 131954-132069, 11:20:02-11:28:45): all normal (received/leased/progress/completed), no retries or setting mentions.

  - Page 9 (seq 132128-132185, 11:32:52-11:35:58): retries proliferate across many jobs (attempts 1-2 of 3), still only generic "worker process ended unexpectedly" message, no setting/value cited.

- Not yet read: pages 4, 5 (seq ~131838-131953, roughly 11:10-11:20) and pages 11-15 (seq 132244 onward, 11:40:12 to end of hour).

- Findings so far: No journal line in basalt-extract's own log (pages 1-3, 6-10) explicitly names a configuration setting or value; all crash/retry/rejection lines use generic phrasing ("worker process ended unexpectedly", "rejected after 3 worker crashes; customer notified"). If none found in these ranges either, may need to reconsider whether such a line exists elsewhere (e.g., different hour, or a one-time startup/reload event near 10:42 when CHG-43068 took effect — check if that falls within the 11:00 hour window or earlier hour journal)."}

parts.content:
playbook: symptom catalogue
  SYM-PAGE-CAP  documents above a certain length are refused at the split stage and rejected  (section: page-cap-rejections)
  SYM-HOOK-DROP  customers stop receiving completion webhooks  (section: webhook-delivery-failures)
  SYM-INDEX-LAG  search results lag behind because the index queue is backed up  (section: index-backlog)
  SYM-LEASE-SHORT  jobs keep returning to the queue before they finish and are eventually rejected  (section: lease-starvation)
  SYM-TENANT-QUOTA  one tenant's jobs are refused because it has reached its quota  (section: tenant-quota)
  SYM-WORKER-MEM  workers die partway through larger documents and the jobs are eventually rejected  (section: worker-memory-exhaustion)
  SYM-SCAN-HOLD  uploads are quarantined by the malware scanner and rejected  (section: scan-quarantine)

playbook: worker-memory-exhaustion (SYM-WORKER-MEM)
what you see: workers die partway through larger documents and the jobs are eventually rejected
procedure:
  P-6.1 (confirm): check the queue statistics and the component's journal for the pattern above
  P-6.2 (contain): pause new uploads for the affected tenants if the backlog keeps growing
  P-6.3 (restore): revert the change that set memory_limit_mb through the change log, then drain the retry queue
  P-6.4 (verify): watch the next two ten-minute rows of the queue statistics return to normal
